items.name: Swiss citizenship

needed_by.purpose: Swiss citizens living in Switzerland are not subject to source tax
Decides whether the permit reminder is shown

items.asked_when: Only if the employee lives in Switzerland and is not a Swiss citizen

needed_by.purpose: Non-Swiss employees with a C permit are treated like Swiss and are not subject to source tax

items.required_when_expr: address_country == "Switzerland" and nationality == "no" and permit_type == "no" and civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"]

needed_by.purpose: A Swiss spouse living in Switzerland exempts the employee from source tax

items.notes: Flow step 5. Separated employees count as single for source tax, so no spouse exemption applies.

items.name: Spouse holds a C permit

items.name: Spouse lives in Switzerland

items.notes: Flow step 5. Two values instead of a full country, because only 'in Switzerland or not' drives the rule (data minimisation).

needed_by.purpose: Church-tax suffix Y / N of the tariff code

items.name: Spouse employed or receiving replacement income

items.name: Children

items.required_when_expr: child_age_status in ["Minor", "Of age and in first education"]

needed_by.purpose: Child counting and H tariff

items.name: Parental custody (child in household)

items.asked_when: For each minor child living in the same household

needed_by.purpose: Sole custody counts the child (H for single employees)

items.name: Common household with the other parent

items.required_when_expr: child_same_household == "yes" and (child_parental_custody == "Shared custody" or child_age_status == "Of age and in first education")

needed_by.purpose: Child counting and H tariff

items.name: Shared custody (child not in household, married)
items.description: For married / partnered employees with a minor child outside the household: whether there is shared custody.
items.asked_when: For each minor child not in the household, if the employee is married or in a registered partnership
items.asked_when_expr: civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"] and child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "no"
items.required_when_expr: civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"] and child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "no"

needed_by.purpose: Child counting

items.name: Parental custody (child not in household, single)
items.description: For single, divorced, widowed or separated employees with a minor child outside the household: whether the employee has parental custody.
items.asked_when: For each minor child not in the household, if the employee is single, divorced, widowed or separated
items.asked_when_expr: civil_status in ["Single", "Divorced", "Widowed", "Separated"] and child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "no"
items.required_when_expr: civil_status in ["Single", "Divorced", "Widowed", "Separated"] and child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "no"

needed_by.purpose: Child counting and H tariff

items.name: Alternating care
items.description: Whether the child is in alternating care between the parents.
items.asked_when: For a minor child in the household with shared custody and no common household with the other parent; or a minor child outside the household with shared custody (married) or parental custody (single)
items.asked_when_expr: (child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "yes" and child_parental_custody == "Shared custody" and child_common_household_other_parent == "no") or (child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "no" and (child_shared_custody_not_in_household == "yes" or child_parental_care_not_in_household == "yes"))
items.required_when_expr: (child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "yes" and child_parental_custody == "Shared custody" and child_common_household_other_parent == "no") or (child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "no" and (child_shared_custody_not_in_household == "yes" or child_parental_care_not_in_household == "yes"))

needed_by.purpose: Child counting and H tariff

items.description: Who makes the larger financial contribution to the child's maintenance: the employee or the other parent.
items.asked_when: If the child is in alternating care; or, for single, divorced, widowed or separated employees, if the child lives in the household and there is a common household with the other parent
items.asked_when_expr: child_alternating_custody == "yes" or (civil_status in ["Single", "Divorced", "Widowed", "Separated"] and child_same_household == "yes" and child_common_household_other_parent == "yes")
items.required_when_expr: child_alternating_custody == "yes" or (civil_status in ["Single", "Divorced", "Widowed", "Separated"] and child_same_household == "yes" and child_common_household_other_parent == "yes")

needed_by.purpose: Child counting and H tariff

items.asked_when_expr: child_age_status == "Of age and in first education" and (child_same_household == "no" or child_common_household_other_parent == "no")
items.required_when_expr: child_age_status == "Of age and in first education" and (child_same_household == "no" or child_common_household_other_parent == "no")

needed_by.purpose: Child counting and H tariff

rules.name: Insurance start date
rules.statement: The pension fund insurance starts on the first working day if that is the 1st of a month; otherwise on the 1st of the following month. Always derived from the latest first working day.

table.then: Insurance starts on the first working day
Insurance starts on the 1st of the following month (e.g. 15.03. → 01.04.)

rules.name: Civil status for the pension fund
rules.statement: The civil status is entered at the pension fund from its list. Provisionally, registered partnership and separated are entered as Married.

table.then: Married (with the partner's date of birth), provisional
Married (with the spouse's date of birth), provisional

rules.name: Civil status for source tax
rules.statement: For source tax, married and registered partnership count as 'married or registered partnership'; single, divorced, separated and widowed count as 'single'.
rules.expression: if_else(civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"], "Married or registered partnership", if_else(civil_status in ["Single", "Divorced", "Widowed", "Separated"], "Single, divorced, separated or widowed", null))

rules.name: Spouse exemption from source tax
rules.statement: A married or registered-partner employee is exempt from source tax if the spouse/partner is Swiss or holds a C permit and lives in Switzerland. Separated employees count as single and get no exemption.
rules.expression: civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"] and (spouse_nationality == "yes" or spouse_permit_type == "yes") and spouse_residence_country == "Switzerland"

rules.name: Subject to source tax
rules.statement: An employee living abroad is always subject to source tax, whatever the nationality. An employee living in Switzerland is subject only if not a Swiss citizen, holding no C permit and not exempted by a Swiss / C-permit spouse living in Switzerland. Only employees subject to source tax are asked the source tax questions.
rules.expression: (address_country != null and address_country != "Switzerland") or (address_country == "Switzerland" and nationality == "no" and permit_type == "no" and not spouse_exempts_source_tax)

rules.name: Source tax state of residence
rules.statement: The calculator's residence answers are derived from the home address country: Switzerland, Germany, Liechtenstein, or another country. Switzerland and another country leave the base tariff unchanged.
rules.expression: if_else(address_country == "Switzerland", "Switzerland", if_else(address_country == "Germany", "Germany", if_else(address_country == "Liechtenstein", "Liechtenstein", if_else(address_country != null, "Other country", null))))

rules.name: Child digit of the tariff code
rules.statement: The digit equals the number of children that count (with or without H). No children or none counting gives 0.

rules.name: Single-parent H tariff
rules.statement: A single, divorced, separated or widowed employee with at least one child counting with H gets the H tariff.
inputs: At least one child counts with H
rules.expression: civil_status in ["Single", "Divorced", "Widowed", "Separated"] and child_tariff_result == "counts with H"

rules.name: Cross-border tariff applies
rules.statement: For employees living in Germany the cross-border tariff applies with daily return and a certificate of residence ('not yet' counts as no), or without daily return when a return is reasonable and not more than 60 non-return days are expected. All other cases use the normal tariff.
rules.expression: subject_to_source_tax and address_country == "Germany" and ((daily_return_germany == "yes" and residence_certificate == "yes") or (daily_return_germany == "no" and daily_return_reasonable == "yes" and non_return_days_60 == "no"))

rules.name: Liechtenstein: in principle no source tax
rules.statement: For employees living in Liechtenstein, daily return or not more than 45 non-return days gives 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement' instead of a tariff code, flagged for HR. More than 45 non-return days gives the normal tariff code subject to the double taxation agreement.

table.then: In principle no source tax liability (flag for HR)
In principle no source tax liability (flag for HR)
Normal tariff code, subject to the double taxation agreement

rules.name: Tariff letter
rules.statement: Married/registered partnership: C (spouse employed) or B; single etc.: H (single-parent) or A. With the cross-border tariff the letter becomes A→L, B→M, C→N, H→P.
rules.expression: if_else(not subject_to_source_tax, null, if_else(civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"], if_else(spouse_employed == "yes", if_else(cross_border_tariff_applies, "N", "C"), if_else(cross_border_tariff_applies, "M", "B")), if_else(single_parent_h_tariff, if_else(cross_border_tariff_applies, "P", "H"), if_else(cross_border_tariff_applies, "L", "A"))))

rules.name: Source tax result
rules.statement: For every employee subject to source tax Lonio computes the tariff code = tariff letter + child digit + church-tax suffix (e.g. C1Y, L0Y) and records it for HR. Liechtenstein residents with daily return or at most 45 non-return days get 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement' instead, flagged for HR. Always recomputed from the latest answers.
inputs: Liechtenstein: in principle no source tax

table.then: No tariff code (not subject to source tax)
'In principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement', flagged for HR
Tariff code, subject to the double taxation agreement
Tariff code (letter + child digit + church-tax suffix)

rules.name: Permit reminder
rules.statement: At the end of the questionnaire, every non-Swiss employee and every employee living abroad is reminded to bring their permit on the first working day. HR words it so a Swiss citizen living abroad sees it does not apply to them. It collects no data.

rules.name: Discard answers that no longer apply
rules.statement: If the employee changes an earlier answer so that later questions no longer apply, those answers are kept while the employee goes back and forth but discarded on submission. After submission the questionnaire is read-only for the employee; changes are made by HR and all derived results are derived again from the latest answers.

open_questions.question: What does Pensionskasse Muster expect in 'Canton' for employees living abroad, and does 'Canton' mean canton of residence or of work?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The field is required and lists only Swiss cantons; employees abroad cannot be registered without an answer.
options: Canton of work (Zurich) for employees abroad
Canton of residence; the fund gives a rule for employees abroad
Canton means work canton for everyone
open_questions.recommendation: Provisionally ask only residents of Switzerland (D-002); verify with a domain expert and the fund.

open_questions.question: How does the pension fund want registered partnerships and separated employees registered (the list has only Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed), and does it want partner details?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A wrong civil status or a missing partner date of birth makes the registration wrong.
options: Keep provisional mapping (both as Married with spouse/partner date of birth)
open_questions.recommendation: Use the provisional mapping (D-003) until a domain expert verifies it.

open_questions.question: Does the fund's screen ask for a spouse's date of birth (or other data) for Divorced or Widowed?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The screenshots show only Single and Married; a hidden required field would block registration.
options: Extra field shown - add a question
open_questions.recommendation: Do not ask divorced/widowed employees (D-004); verify with a screenshot of the fund's screen.

open_questions.question: Does Lonio's computed tariff code match the calculator on paths not explored: residence block for A/B/H tariffs, more than 3 children, H3N/P3N, and the child paths marked 'inferred' in the child result table?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Lonio now owns the tariff result; an unverified path could produce a wrong tariff code.
options: Domain expert compares computed codes with the calculator before go-live
